newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanians take election battle into cyberspace.
newsitem.headline: Romanians take election battle into cyberspace.

text.p: Computer freaks forayed into Romania's presidential election campaign and picked an early winner, replacing incumbent Ion Iliescu on the Internet with his rival, local media reported on Wednesday.

A portrait of Emil Constantinescu, the president's centrist opponent, was flashed on the government's home page on the Net instead of Iliescu's picture as president of Romania, the top-selling daily Evenimentul Zilei said.
The switch of presidents, engineered by anonymous hackers in the run-up to Sunday's run-off vote, had been remedied by nightfall, according to Net surfers contacted by Reuters.
Iliescu, an ex-communist in power since the fall of communism 1989, faces a tough battle against Constantinescu, a professor with no political career under the Communists.
An "Internet Cafe" recently opened in Bucharest is a hangout for many Romanian youths who can play the information superhighway for the equivalent of less than a dollar.
